chunks: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani informed us from 'Ali b. al-Hasan b. 'Ali b. Faddal from his father from Abu'l Hasan 'Ali b. Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said:

Whoever shuns striving for his needs on the day of Ashura, God will fulfill his needs of this world and the Hereafter. And whoever makes the day of Ashura a day of his calamity, his grief, and his weeping, God, Mighty and Majestic, will make the Day of Resurrection a day of his joy and his delight, and his eye shall be cooled by us in the Gardens.

And whoever calls the day of Ashura a day of blessing and stores anything in his household on it, what he has stored will not be blessed for him, and he will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection with Yazid, 'Ubaydullah b. Ziyad, and 'Umar b. Sa'd (may God curse them) in the lowest pit of the Fire.

key_terms.أسفل درك من النار: the lowest pit of the Fire — the deepest level of hellfire, reserved for the worst transgressors
key_terms.عاشوراء: Ashura — the 10th of Muharram, anniversary of the martyrdom of Imam Husayn at Karbala
key_terms.قرت عينه: his eye was cooled — an Arabic expression meaning consolation and happiness
key_terms.يوم القيامة: Day of Resurrection — the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about mourning on Ashura?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) teaches about the spiritual significance of Ashura, the 10th of Muharram, when Imam Husayn was martyred at Karbala in 680 CE. He prescribes three responses: abandoning worldly pursuits leads to divine fulfillment, mourning earns paradise, while treating it as a day of celebration leads to companionship with Husayn's killers in hellfire. This hadith was narrated in the context of the assembly convened on the first of Muharram, making it directly relevant to the approaching commemoration.
